classification.difficultyReason: Use supplied semitone and tuning ratios, compare frequencies by subtraction, and convert an explicitly specified mean of logarithms into a geometric mean.

content.prompt: [Keyboard tuning] When a keyboard is tuned to modern concert pitch, the note A below middle C vibrates at $220\text{ Hz}$ (1 hertz is 1 vibration per second), and the note A′ above middle C vibrates at twice that frequency, which is $440\text{ Hz}$ (these names are not standard, but are convenient for this question). When modern *equal temperament* is used for the twelve semitones of the scale from A and A′, the frequency ratio of each semitone is $2^{1/12}$, so that on a logarithmic scale base 10, the log of all the semitones ratios is $\frac{1}{12}\log_{10}2$. Give non-exact numerical answers correct to two decimal places.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find, correct to two decimal places, the frequencies of C, C♯ and E, if the interval AC consists of three semitones, A C♯ of four semitones, and AE of seven semitones.

answer.worked:
After $n$ semitones, the frequency is $220(2^{1/12})^n=220\times2^{n/12}$ Hz.

$$\begin{align*}f_C&=220\times2^{3/12}\approx261.63\text{ Hz}\\f_{C\sharp}&=220\times2^{4/12}\approx277.18\text{ Hz}\\f_E&=220\times2^{7/12}\approx329.63\text{ Hz}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Unfortunately, intervals sound best when their ratios consist of small whole numbers, as most of them are in *meantone temperament*, the most common temperament from say 1500 to 1800. Using that temperament, find the frequencies of C, C♯ and E, if the interval AC is in the ratio $6:5$ (meaning frequency of C : frequency of A $=6:5$), A C♯ is in ratio $5:4$, and AE is in ratio $3:2$.

answer.short: C: $264\text{ Hz}$; C♯: $275\text{ Hz}$; E: $330\text{ Hz}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: When two frequencies close together are sounded together, there is an ugly *beat frequency*, which is the difference between the frequencies. Calculate the beat frequencies between the equal-tempered and meantone versions of C, C♯ and E.

answer.worked:
Use the absolute difference, keeping the equal-tempered frequencies unrounded.

$$\begin{align*}b_C&=\left|264-220\times2^{3/12}\right|\approx2.37\text{ Hz}\\b_{C\sharp}&=\left|275-220\times2^{4/12}\right|\approx2.18\text{ Hz}\\b_E&=\left|330-220\times2^{7/12}\right|\approx0.37\text{ Hz}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Meantone temperament is actually very complicated. Suppose that a careless tuner tuned A at $220\text{ Hz}$, then tuned three major thirds so that A C♯ was in ratio $5:4$, C♯ F was in ratio $5:4$, and F A′ was in ratio $5:4$. What would the resulting frequency of A′ be, and how would it beat with A′ tuned to $440\text{ Hz}$ on another instrument?

answer.short:
A′: $429.69\text{ Hz}$; beat frequency: $10.31\text{ Hz}$.

Multiply by $\frac54$ for each of the three major thirds, then take the frequency difference.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f_{A'}&=220\left(\frac54\right)^3\\f_{A'}&=\frac{6875}{16}=429.6875\text{ Hz}\\f_{A'}&\approx429.69\text{ Hz}\\b&=\left|440-\frac{6875}{16}\right|\\b&=\frac{165}{16}\approx10.31\text{ Hz}\end{align*}$$

The tuned A′ is lower than $440\text{ Hz}$ and produces about $10.31$ beats per second.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Meantone temperament gets its name from the fact that B between A and C♯ is tuned so that the log of its frequency is the mean of the logs of the frequencies of A and C♯ (B is two semitones above A, and two semitones below C♯). Find the meantone frequency of B, and the equal-temperament frequency of B.

answer.short:
Meantone: $245.97\text{ Hz}$; equal temperament: $246.94\text{ Hz}$.

The mean of the logarithms gives the geometric mean of the frequencies.
answer.worked:
Let $f_B$ be the meantone frequency of B, in Hz. From part b, the meantone frequency of C♯ is $275\text{ Hz}$.

$$\begin{align*}\log_{10}f_B&=\frac{\log_{10}220+\log_{10}275}{2}\\\log_{10}f_B&=\frac12\log_{10}(220\times275)\\\log_{10}f_B&=\log_{10}\sqrt{220\times275}\\f_B&=\sqrt{220\times275}=110\sqrt5\\f_B&\approx245.97\text{ Hz}\end{align*}$$

For equal temperament, B is two semitones above A:

$$\begin{align*}f_{B,\mathrm{equal}}&=220\times2^{2/12}\\f_{B,\mathrm{equal}}&\approx246.94\text{ Hz}.\end{align*}$$
